I have been farming for 40 years. I never went to school, but I know this land. I watch what my neighbors do, and if their wheat looks good, I do the same thing.

I have 16.9 mu. I put 8 mu in wheat-maize because that is what this land is good for. The other 8.9 mu I split into 5 mu cotton and 3.9 mu chili. I tried last year and the year before, and this works.

For **wheat** on 8 mu: I rotary till before sowing in October. I buy improved seed, the kind they sell at the cooperative. I put one big bag of compound fertilizer on each mu before sowing — that is 100 jin per mu. Then at green-up time I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 40 jin per mu. I irrigate 3 times: once in winter, twice in spring. I spray 4 times for weeds and bugs. Last year I got 1000 jin per mu. I will do the same this year. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. A bad harvest means my family loses money.

For **maize** on the same 8 mu: After we cut wheat in June, I do not till. The machine sows maize directly. I use hybrid seed, Denghai 605. I put about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing. Two irrigations is enough — one when it is small, one at big flare. Three sprays for bugs and weeds. I expect 1100 jin per mu. My neighbor got 1200 jin last year with the same seed, so I am doing it right.

For **cotton** on 5 mu: I rotary till in April. I use improved cotton seed. One bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu, about 100 jin. Cotton needs a lot of spraying — I spray 14 times for bollworms and other insects. I irrigate twice. Last year I got 550 jin per mu. The price was okay.

For **chili** on 3.9 mu: Chili makes money but it eats fertilizer and medicine. I rotary till and plant in spring. I use improved seed. I put two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — 100 jin at planting, then another 100 jin later. I also add one bag of urea and some potash fertilizer because chili needs it, otherwise the peppers are small. I irrigate 4 times. I spray 21 times because aphids and mites love chili. Last year I harvested 5500 jin per mu. It is a lot of work, but it pays.

I do what I did last year. Change is risky. I see my neighbors applying about the same, so I know this is right.
